To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transition to junior and middle school was accompanied by changes in the classroom environment that are consistent with the hypothesis that the transition is accompanied by changes in students' needs for social interaction and for autonomy.

1) the transition to junior-high school is accompanied by a significant change in the classroom environment; 2) the change in the classroom is in a direction that is not conducive to the development of a sense of personal responsibility and self-direction among students; 3) the change in classroom organization is accompanied by a deterioration in the relationship between teachers and students; 4) the deterioration in the relationship is not accompanied by an increase in the use of social comparisons; and 5) the transition
the classroom environments experienced by students before and after the junior high school transition are not developmentally matched.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the transition from elementary school to junior high school upon the classroom environment.
the classroom environment as it relates to student and teacher behaviors.
the transition to junior-high school and the effects of the transition on students and teachers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the classroom environments of junior high school are more competitive, teacher-centered, and impersonal than those of elementary school.
the transition to junior (or middle school) is a time of change in the classroom environment and that these changes are not always in the direction of a more student-oriented environment.
junior high school classrooms are not as good as elementary school classrooms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the classroom environment in junior high school is less conducive to the development of self-regulated learning than that in elementary school. (Author/RL)
students are not given the same opportunities for interaction, cooperation, and input into classroom tasks after the transition.

, in comparison with the elementary classroom, the junior high school classroom is less student-centered, more teacher-dominated, more competitive, more oriented toward individual performance, less oriented toward group work, and less likely to provide opportunities for student input and participation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transition to junior secondary school is a critical time in the life course of young people.
students' perceptions of their classrooms change dramatically as they move from elementary to middle schools.
teachers and students need to be more aware of the classroom environment.
